_meta.indication: GIVLAARI is indicated for the treatment of adults with acute hepatic porphyria (AHP).
_meta.receipt_date: June 4, 2019 (NDA dated and received June 4, 2019; earlier submissions November 15, 2018 and January 22, 2019)

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized (1:1), multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled study with a 6-month double-blind period and an open-label extension.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients ≥ 12 years with documented AIP or non-AIP AHP (HCP, VP, ADP) and active disease with at least 2 porphyria attacks within the 6 months prior to screening.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: annualized rate of porphyria attacks (AAR) requiring hospitalization, urgent care visit, or in-home IV hemin administration, in AIP patients.
pivotal_trials.n: 94 AHP patients randomized (48 givosiran, 46 placebo); 89 were AIP (primary analysis set).
pivotal_trials.result: Study met its primary endpoint: annualized AAR 3.9 with givosiran vs 14.3 with placebo; patients on givosiran experienced 70% (95% CI 53%, 84%) fewer attacks (rate ratio 0.27; 95% CI 0.16, 0.47).

key_safety: Most common AEs (≥5% more than placebo): nausea (27% vs 11%), injection site reactions (25% vs 0%), rash (17% vs 4%), increased serum creatinine (15% vs 4%), increased hepatic transaminases (13% vs 2%), fatigue (10% vs 4%). SAEs in 21% givosiran vs 9% placebo; anaphylaxis reported in 1/111 (1%) patients. Key risks: injection site reactions, renal toxicity, hepatotoxicity, and anaphylaxis.
target_moa: Givosiran is a double-stranded small interfering RNA (siRNA) that causes degradation of ALAS1 mRNA in hepatocytes through RNA interference, reducing neurotoxic ALA and PBG and subsequent porphyria attacks.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee.

summary.text: Givosiran (GIVLAARI) received Priority review as an NDA, with prior Orphan drug designation (August 29, 2016) and Breakthrough therapy designation (May 23, 2017) for AHP; approval was based on the single pivotal ENVISION trial and was not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: August 29, 2016: Orphan designation for the treatment of acute hepatic porphyria (AHP).
May 23, 2017: Breakthrough therapy designation for the prophylaxis of attacks in patients with AHP.
The single pivotal ENVISION study supports the proposed indication for givosiran for the treatment of adult patients with AHP.

requirement.text: PMC 3743-1: Conduct a controlled trial in pediatric patients (age ≥ 12 to < 17 years) with AHP to evaluate dose, clinical outcomes, and safety of givosiran.

citations.quote: 3743-1 Conduct a controlled trial in pediatric patients to evaluate the dose, clinical outcomes, and safety of givosiran for the treatment of pediatric patients age greater than or equal to 12 years to less than 17 years with acute hepatic porphyria. Appropriate sampling must be incorporated to explore exposure-response relationships for measures of pharmacodynamic biomarkers, safety, and efficacy. The final protocol should be agreed upon with the Agency.
